content.title: Response to Reviewer adcw (1/3)
content.comment:
Thanks for the comments. We would like to emphasize that in this paper we focus on the source-free universal domain adaptation problem, ***we will further stress this in the text, also with regard to the used definition of open-partial and universal DA***. Incorporating a simple DA method, by means of our newly **proposed weighted entropy minimization (instead of normal entropy minimization)** is enough to achieve SOTA results. If we instead combine it with a more complex DA method, like AaD (**note AaD is added into the proposed weighted entropy minimization**) we show that results can be even further improved. **And we attach our code in the newly uploaded supplementary material.**
 
 
 
1. The authors are strongly suggested to report results on closed-set or partial-set UDA datasets and compare them with most existing source data-free UDA methods
 
This paper aims to address domain shift problem under category shift, in other words, the problem where there exists open classes during adaptation. And in our paper, we use the term universal DA as identical to Open-Partial Domain Adaptation (such as [2,4]). We also stress this in the footnote on page 4. However, we agree with the reviewer that it would be interesting to see the closed-set DA results (and will add these results shown in the table below to the Appendix). For a fair comparison, we only compare to other open-set or universal domain adaptation methods**. The results still show the effectiveness of our method. 
We have excluded closed-set DA methods from the comparison, since these methods exploit the prior knowledge that no new classes are present, and therefore will obtain better results, **but those closed-set methods cannot work for neither open-set nor universal domain adaptation**. We also attach the results on open-set DA. **Note only our method is source-free**.

content.title: Response to Reviewer adcw (2/3)
content.comment:
2. the objective in Eq.(2) is hard to understand. what if the weight is set to 1 for different batches?
 
 
The weight in Eq. 2 will be decided by the predicted known/unknown ratio in the mini-batch (or alternatively the ratio over the whole dataset which achieves similar results as shown in the appendix). If using the predicted known/unknown ratio in the mini-batch as weight, weight in Eq. 2 (for mini-batch) will turn into $\frac{1}{n_k^\*}$ and $\frac{1}{n_u^\*}$, where $n_k^\*$ is the number of samples predicted as known class ***in the mini-batch***, $n_u^\*$ is the number of samples predicted as unknown class ***in the mini-batch***.
It works as a dynamic weight to balance the updating gradient for known and unknown categories. Since there typically exists a known/unknown imbalance problem, in either the mini-batch or the whole dataset, the updating signal from known or unknown should be balanced. We actually have an ablation study on the weight in "Importance of weight in entropy minimization" in the experiment section. If setting the weight to 1, it will only get 32.1% on R2C on Office-Home (while with the proposed weight it will get 63.9%), it shows the proposed simple weight entropy minimization works well for the imbalanced situation, **using this weight for entropy minimizing is one of the contributions of the paper**.
 
 
#### Ablation study (R2C of Office-Home) on the proposed weight in the weighted entropy minimization. Results of OVANet are from our running based on their official code.
| R2C                         | OS*  | UNK  | OS   | H    |
| --------------------------- | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| w/o weight in Eq.2          | 19.2 | 97.8 | 26.3 | 32.1 |
| w/ weight in Eq.2 (OneRing) | 57.8 | 71.6 | 59.1 | 63.9 |
 
 
 
 
3. Evaluation metric: H/OS/OS*/UNK
 
For the evaluation metric, we report exactly the same metric (H, or both H and OS) following the most recent UNDA works. Specifically, all those methods [1,2,3,4,5] only report H (harmonic mean between known and unknown accuracy, $H=\frac{2\times{{OS}^*}\times{UNK}}{{{OS}^*}+{UNK}}$
) on VisDA and Office-Home, few of them [4] report OS on Office-31, **we report exactly the same metric scores as those papers (***especially [2] is the current SOTA universal DA method***), showing the effectiveness of our methods**. As discussed by ROS [6] and OVANet [2], considering the trade-off between the accuracy of known and unknown classes is important in evaluating universal or open-set DA methods. The OS metric (average accuracy over all classes) is problematic, as many methods with high OS have poor open-class recognition performance, since $OS=\frac{|\mathcal{C}_s|}{|\mathcal{C}_s| + 1} \times {OS}^*+ \frac{1}{|\mathcal{C}_s| + 1} \times {UNK}$, a method even with 0 UNK accuracy can have quite high OS, as shown in the table below. **Only when both OS\* and UNK are higher, and the difference between OS\* and UNK is small, results in a high H value**. As the goal of UNDA is to detect open classes, as well as recognizing known classes, H is currently, in our opinion, the best available metric to evaluate these methods. H value can not be high if only one of the OS\* and UNK is high, since it is the harmonic mean. The high UNK value in the paper exactly proves the effectiveness of the proposed simple methods. **We also show OS\*, UNK, OS and H on VisDA in the table below, compared to the recent SOTA UNDA method OVANet, the results further prove the effectiveness of our method.**
 
 
#### Open-set DA on Office-Home, results are from [6], signifying OS metric is problematic
| ODA/UNDA methods | OS*  | UNK  | OS   | H    |
| ---------------- | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| STA              | 63.4 | 62.6 | 63.4 | 61.9 |
| OSBP             | 64.1 | 66.3 | 64.2 | 64.7 |
| UAN              | 75.2 | 0.0  | 72.3 | 0    |
 
#### Open-partial DA on VisDA, results of OVANet are from our running based on their code
| VisDA     | source-free | OS*  | UNK  | OS   | H    |
| --------- | ----------- | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| OVANet    | $\times$    | 60.5 | 46.4 | 58.5 | 52.5 |
| OneRing-S |             | 25.7 | 55.9 | 30.0 | 35.2 |
| OneRing   | $\surd$     | 57.2 | 64.6 | 58.3 | 60.7 |
| OneRing+  | $\surd$     | 65.5 | 66.8 | 65.7 | 66.1 |

content.title: Response to Reviewer adcw (3/3)
content.comment:
4. the UNK score is always very high for the proposed method, which makes the largest contribution of the impressive H-score. The proposed method is hard to improve the adaptation performance.
 
1) **The results shown in Tab. 2-4 are not for domain adaptation, but for open-set domain generalization, all methods in those tables except ours are explicitly using a domain generalization technique. Our method does not have any process for neither adaptation nor generalization. As mentioned in the paper, the results here (high UNK) are only to show the strong open-set recognition ability of our method even under domain shift. And as discussed above, H value can not be high if only one of the OS\* and UNK is high, since it is the harmonic mean.**
 
2) We respectfully disagree with the comment that “the proposed training strategy is hard to improve the adaptation performance”. As mentioned above, the H value can well evaluate the performance, since only when known accuracy OS* and unknown accuracy UNK are both high, this leads to a high H. The proposed **weight entropy minimization** significantly improves both OS* and UNK, as shown in "Importance of weight in entropy minimization" in the experiment section, **and also shown in the table below, which clearly proves that the proposed weighted entropy minimization works well for adaptation.** Adding closed-set tailored method AaD into the proposed weighted entropy minimization further improves the results on both OS* and UNK. Also, the improvement on OS* from source model to OneRing proves the effectiveness of the adaptation by the weighted entropy minimization.
 
 
 
#### Ablation study (R2C of Office-Home) on the proposed weight in the weighted entropy minimization. Results of OVANet are from our running based on their official code.
| R2C                         | OS*  | UNK  | OS   | H    |
| --------------------------- | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| OVANet                      | 55.1 | 70.0 | 56.5 | 61.7 |
| w/o weight in Eq.2          | 19.2 | 97.8 | 26.3 | 32.1 |
| w/ weight in Eq.2 (OneRing) | 57.8 | 71.6 | 59.1 | 63.9 |
| + AaD   (OneRing+)          | 61.5 | 82.7 | 63.4 | 70.5 |
 
 
 
 
5. Misc
 
The reviewer is right about the results in Tab. 2-4. **We would like to point out that those results in Table 3-4 are directly copied from [7] (ICLR 2022), where H is copied from tables in the main paper (their Tab. 3-4), and UNK and OS\* are copied from other different tables in the appendix (their Tab. 8-9), the authors of [7] may run different experiments for H and UNK/OS\*, this could be the reason for the noted discrepancy. We emailed the authors for inquiry but have not yet received any answer.** For DomainNet, note that OneRing is already enough to achieve good performance. And this is a huge dataset, and adding AaD will demand large computing capacity as AaD builds two memory banks and needs to retrieve nearest neighbors. We try adding OneRing into the weighted entropy minimization by using the same hyperparameters of AaD as VisDA, the improvement is only 0.3\%, we posit tuning the 2 hyperparameters could further improve the results, we leave this for future work since this is not the key part of our method.
 
### reference

[1] Universal Domain Adaptation through Self Supervision. NeurIPS 2020\
[2] OVANet: One-vs-All Network for Universal Domain Adaptation. ICCV 2021\
[3] Domain Consensus Clustering for Universal Domain Adaptation. CVPR 2021\
[4] Learning to detect open classes for universal domain adaptation. ECCV 2020\
[5] Unified Optimal Transport Framework for Universal Domain Adaptation. NeurIPS 2022\
[6] On the Effectiveness of Image Rotation for Open Set Domain Adaptation. ECCV 2020\
[7] CROSSMATCH: CROSS-CLASSIFIER CONSISTENCY REGULARIZATION FOR OPEN-SET SINGLE DOMAIN GENERALIZATION. ICLR 2022

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper investigated the problem of universal domain adaptation or open-partial domain adaptation under the source-free setting. The authors proposed a novel training scheme called OneRing where an (n+1)-way classifier was learned with only source domain data. OneRing was used to empower the source-trained model with the ability of unknown class recognition. The authors further proposed a weighted entropy minimization objective to adapt the source model to the target domain. Empirical evaluations on open-set recognition, open-set single-domain generalization, and source-free universal domain adaptation proved the efficacy and generalization ability of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strengths
1. The OneRing training scheme is novel and interesting.
2. The proposed method including OneRing and the weighted entropy objective, is simple and easy to implement.
3. Empirical results on various tasks and benchmarks support the efficacy and generalization of the proposed method.

## Weaknesses
1. Though simple yet effective, the proposed method is not well explained or motivated. What essential qualities does OneRing encourage beneficial for open-set recognition? Why is it necessary to re-weight the entropy minimization term for known and unknown samples? The presentation in the methodology part (Section 3.2- 3.3) seems to plainly describe the steps of the proposed method. Analysis and ablation experiments in Section 4 also only show the efficacy and good results of the method without either intuitive understanding or theoretical analysis.

2. Missing technical details: 1). What is the batch size of different tasks? How do weights in Eq. 2 change during the training? Because these directly affect the batch-level weighted entropy minimization objective. 2). Why did OneRing underperform other open-set recognition methods on the PACS benchmark which has the least category number? 3). Why did the method fail to converge on DomainNet, as was mentioned in Section 4.2?

3. All domain adaptation experiments in the submission belong to the open-partial setting. How does the method perform on open-set domain adaptation, since Table 1 also covers this setting?

4. Typo: "target date" in Table 1 caption.

4. Missing related works: 
1). UMAD: Universal Model Adaptation under Domain and Category Shift, arXiv:2112.08553
2). Open-set Hypothesis Transfer with Semantic Consistency. IEEE Transactions on Image Processing

## Post-rebuttal Rating

I have read all reviews and responses and discussed them with the authors. The authors did not address my concern about the overclaimed contributions, misleading problem settings, and the reliability of the experiments. 
Although the authors replied that they have already revised the paper to address the above concerns, I find the up-to-date revision still has remaining problems. For example, in the abstract, UNDA was mentioned without any explanation. Throughout the whole context, there are still mixed uses of OPDA and UNDA, which is confusing. Besides, the authors still cannot ensure the correctness and fairness of experimental comparisons.

From my perspective, this submission requires careful revision to avoid misleading claims and unreliable experimental results before being accepted to a top venue. As a result, I would not recommend a paper without a careful check on claims and experimental results. I will decrease my final score to 5.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. Clarity. This paper is easy-to-follow and well-organized. 
2. Quality. The methodology is not well motivated and explained. The experiments are comprehensive, including various tasks and benchmarks. 
3. Novelty. As for the proposed method, the OneRing training scheme is novel and the weighted entropy minimization objective is a commonly used term. 
4. Reproducibility. No codes are provided and no implementation details are provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposed a simple yet effective method for source-free universal domain adaptation. Various experiments proved the efficacy of the open-set recognition ability of OneRing. However, in the current stage, my main concern lies in why the proposed method works and not works in some cases.

content.title: Response to Reviewer kKkf (1/2)
content.comment:
Thanks for the comments, below are our response and **code is already attached**.

1. How OneRing works to detect open classes
 
In OneRing, we have a $C_s + 1$ -way classifier where the final dimension is for the unknown category. Since we do not have any data from unknown categories for training, assigning the second maximal logits to the unknown in the $C_s + 1$ -way classifier (Eq. 1) can effectively avoid bias towards seen class. In Eq. 1, the training can be actually divided into 2 parts: the first part is the normal training with CE loss, another part is to train an open-class detector ($C_s$ -way classifier by *removing the ground truth class dimension*), the sample from the corresponding ground truth category needs to be classified as the unknown category instead of any wrong category. Through this way, we can train a classifier with open-set recognition ability without any sample of open class.
In other view, the training in Eq. 1 will leave out a certain region in the feature space (or classifier weight as prototype) for the future unseen category, as indicated in Fig. 1 (Right). We also have a video in the supplementary material, showing the evolving of the decision boundary during the whole training process. 
 
2. Why using weight in entropy minimizing in Eq. 2, and technic details
 
We attached the code in the newly uploaded supplementary material. As mentioned in experiment details in page 7, our code is based on OVANet. The batch size is 64 for all experiments. The weight in Eq. 2 will be decided by the predicted known/unknown ratio in the mini-batch, it works as a dynamic weight to balance the updating gradient for known and unknown categories, since there typically exists know/unknown imbalance problem in either the mini-batch or the whole dataset, the updating signal from known or unknown should be balanced. **And the results in the paper show that the proposed simple weight entropy minimization can address the imbalance quite well**. We have an ablation study on the weight in "Importance of weight in entropy minimization" in the experiment section to show the importance of the weight, **and also shown in the table below, which clearly shows that the proposed weighted entropy minimization works well for adaptation.**



#### Ablation study on the proposed weight in the weighted entropy minimization
| OS*/UNK/H    | R2C    |
| ----------------  | ---- |
| w/o weight in Eq.2        | 19.2/97.8/32.1 |
| w/ weight in Eq.2      | 57.8/71.6/63.9 |

content.title: Response to Reviewer kKkf (2/2)
content.comment:
3. Why did OneRing underperform other open-set recognition methods on the PACS benchmark which has the least category number.  Why did the method fail to converge on DomainNet.
 
First, we would like to emphasize that Tab. 2-4 are for open-set **domain generalization** problem, and all methods **except ours** have specific modules for domain generalization, "+CM" in the tables means using generated unknown samples along with the specific domain generalization method. In Eq. 1, we could use extra weight to trade off those two CE loss term to further improve the performance, since if the training signal from the first CE loss is too high, the resulting bias towards known categories will deteriorate the open-set recognition ability; in turn if the training signal of the second term is too high, it will degrade the known accuracy on the current training data, which should also be avoided. In PACS we found the trade-off between the 2 CE loss in Eq. 1 can influence results significantly. Assigning a small weight factor (0.7) to the second CE loss in Eq. 1 can improve the final average result over all tasks of OneRing-S from 41.5 to 44.0. ***We did not include this result in the paper trying to keep the simplicity of our method, by avoiding introducing hyperparameters.*** Fig. 4 show the results with different weight factors in Eq. 1 on PACS.
 
DomainNet is a huge dataset compared to other benchmarks, we found if training with the original Eq. 1 during source training, the accuracy of known classes on the training (source) data will increase quite slowly. Thus we propose to first training with only the normal CE loss, and then add the second CE loss for training, this training scheme demands fewer epochs. An alternative solution is also to assign a small weight factor to the second CE loss in Eq. 1, but it will introduce an extra hyperparameter.
 
4. Results on open-set domain adaptation
 
We report results on open-set domain adaptation below.
 
#### Open-set DA on Office-31 (VGG19), results (H) except ours are from OVANet

| ***ODA/UnDA methods*** | ***source-free*** | A2D  | A2W  | D2A  | D2W  | W2D  | W2A  | Avg      |

| ROS                    | $\times$          | 79.0 | 81.0 | 78.1 | 94.4 | 99.7 | 74.1 | 84.4     |

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a novel SF-UNDA method that comprises training an open-set recognition model with the source data and its adaptation to the target data without access to the source domain. For the former training, the authors propose a simple but effective extension to the standard cross-entropy loss to make the model be able to identify unknown-class data. In the adaptation phase, the trained model is fine-tuned with the target data via a weighted entropy minimization. Experimental results with several benchmark datasets show that the proposed method works well in SF-UNDA task as well as OS-SDG task.

- In spite of its simpleness, the proposed method performs well in SF-UNDA as well as OS-SDG.

content.title: Response to Reviewer ymBi
content.comment:
Thanks for the comments, below are our response and **code is already attached**.

1. It is not clear to see why the proposed loss function in Eq. (1) is effective for OS-SDG
 
Instead of improving domain generalization ability, Eq. (1) only aims to recognize open classes. The results for OS-SDG in Tab. 2-4 show: 1) OneRing-S usually does not achieve the best performance on OS* (accuracy on known classes), ***since we do not have any process for domain generalization***; 2) OneRing usually achieves good UNK (unknown) accuracy, showing its effectiveness to distinguish open categories *even under domain shift*. We report the results of OS-SDG not to prove the ability to generalize, but simply to show the resulting model could be a good start for SF-UNDA, as it could detect open classes under domain and category shift. And the reviewer may be right that the reason why OneRing-S has lower known accuracy, is that any other domain data may be classified to UNK. 
 
2. importance of proposed weighted entropy minimizing for adaptation
 
We would like to emphasize the importance of the proposed weighted entropy minimization (Eq. 2), since it is not the normal entropy minimization. The weight here is decided by the predicted known/unknown ratio in the current batch, it is to balance the update signal from the imbalance known and unknown categories, since there typically exists know/unknown imbalance problem in either the mini-batch or the whole dataset, **and the results in the paper show that the proposed simple weight entropy minimization can address the imbalance quite well**. We actually have an ablation study on the weight in "Importance of weight in entropy minimization" in the experiment section to show the importance of the weight, as the normal entropy minimization gets poor performance (32.1% versus our 63.9% on R2C on Office-Home).
 
 
 
 
3. AaD related questions
 
We will add more details of AaD in the appendix. Note here in the classifier we only have one dimension for unknown categories (only one unknown category, but with multiple known classes), it will be problematic to put diversity loss $L_{div}$ on the samples predicted as unknown. We found if adding $L_{div}$ to UNK samples, the results will be quite lower, for example on R2C on Office-Home it will only get 49.1% of H (versus 70.5% with OneRing+).

content.title: General response to all reviewers
content.comment:
1. This paper addresses ***source-free universal*** (open-partial) domain adaptation problem. Compared to existing UNDA methods which are usually complex, we propose a simple yet effective method to achieve adaptation, ***without access to source data during target adaptation***.
 
2. Our proposed method has 2 parts. First the proposed training manner in Eq. 1 empowers the source model with good performance on open class recognition (even under domain shift). Based on the (source) model with great unknown category detection ability, **we show that directly adopting the known and unknown prediction from the current model, a simple weighted entropy minimization is enough to achieve SOTA performance compared to existing *complex* UNDA methods *demanding source data***. The weight here is computed by the predicted known and unknown class ration in each mini-batch or over the whole dataset, **in order to deal with known/unknown imbalance problem**, **This is also a contribution of the paper.** We have an ablation study on the weight in "Importance of weight in entropy minimization" in the experiment section to show the importance of the weight, as the normal entropy minimization gets poor performance.
 
3. For the evaluation metric, **we report exactly the same metric (H, or both H and OS) following the all recent UNDA works in the community**. Specifically, **all those methods [1,2,3,4,5] only report H** (harmonic mean between known and unknown accuracy, $H=\frac{2\times{{OS}^*}\times{UNK}}{{{OS}^*}+{UNK}}$) **on VisDA and Office-Home, few of them [4] report OS on Office-31**. As discussed by ROS [6], OS metric (average accuracy over all classes) is problematic, as many methods with high OS have poor open-class recognition performance, since $OS=\frac{|C_s|}{|C_s| + 1} \times {OS}^*+ \frac{1}{|\mathcal{C}_s| + 1} \times {UNK}$, method even with 0 UNK accuracy can have quite high OS. **Only both OS\* and UNK are higher, along with that the difference between OS\* and UNK is small, can result in a high H value**. As the goal of UNDA is to recognize open classes, and do adaptation for known classes, H is a reasonable metric for evaluation, **since considering the trade-off between the accuracy of known and unknown classes is important in evaluating universal or open-set DA methods**. **The high UNK value in the paper exactly proves the effectiveness of the proposed simple methods.**
 
4. **We attach our code in the newly uploaded supplementary material.**
 
 
#### reference
[1] Universal Domain Adaptation through Self Supervision. NeurIPS 2020\
[2] OVANet: One-vs-All Network for Universal Domain Adaptation. ICCV 2021\
[3] Domain Consensus Clustering for Universal Domain Adaptation. CVPR 2021\
[4] Learning to detect open classes for universal domain adaptation. ECCV 2020\
[5] Unified Optimal Transport Framework for Universal Domain Adaptation. NeurIPS 2022\
[6] On the Effectiveness of Image Rotation for Open Set Domain Adaptation. ECCV 2020

content.title: Results in Tab. 2-4
content.comment:
We would like to emphasize that the results in Tab. 2-4 are for domain generalization, **all other methods have extra module for domain generalization (while we do not have), which is the reason that they have high OS\***. The results here are only to show that our method can detect open classes even under domain shift.


And the results for OS\*/UNK and H in Tab. 3-4 are copied from different tables from [1] (H from their Tab. 3-4, and OS\*/UNK from their Tb. 8-9), their results seem to be indeed problematic, as H, which is the harmonic mean between OS\* and UNK, does not correspond to OS\*/UNK. Since [1] does not release the code, we already emailed the authors of [1] in last week, but do not get response yet. In these tables, we follow the same experimental setting in [1] (dataset splitting, and model details), and report our results, please note that our OneRing-S is just a source model trained with CE losses. Our code is based on the official code of OVANet[2], and we already attached the code and the anonymous link to the checkpoints in the supplementary material.

display_title: Summary of the reviews and responses

content.title: Summary of the reviews and responses
content.comment:
The reviewers mainly have two concerns, here we summarize the concerns and our response below:

> Evaluation metric: known accuracy *OS\**, unknown accuracy *UNK*, average category accuracy *OS*.

We follow the exactly same experiment setting, including the evaluation metric, as **almost all published papers for universal/open-partial DA [1,2,3,4,5,6,7] in recent 2 years, which all only report H (except [8] only report OS), and a few of them report OS on Office-31 as ours)**. As these works already discussed that OS is problematic, since $OS=\frac{|\mathcal{C}_s|}{|\mathcal{C}_s| + 1} \times {OS}^*+ \frac{1}{|\mathcal{C}_s| + 1} \times {UNK}$ where OS can be high even UNK is 0. To address the concern of the reviewers, in our response, we also attach the OS*, UNK, and H of our method along with the source model, to prove the effectiveness of our method. As no methods in open-partial DA report OS* (corresponding to Tab 5,6,7), it is unreasonable to conclude that our method is expected to have lower OS*, as we already show in our response that our method (OneRing) has higher OS* than source model (OneRing-S), so our method is not achieving higher UNK at the price of OS*. More importantly, trade-off between
the accuracy of known (OS*) and unknown (UNK) classes is important in evaluating universal or open-set DA methods, in order words, OS* and UNK are of equal importance in open-partial DA.

> Lower OS* (known accuracy), and problematic results in Tab. 2,3,4

First, results of Tab 2-4, which are for open-set domain generalization, are taken from another ICLR 2022 paper [8], we emailed the authors for the reason as the results are not consistent (H is not consistent with the UNK and OS* as pointed out by Reviewer adcw). Second, all other methods in the tables have complex modules for both domain generalization (responsible for OS*), and open-set recognition under domain shift (responsible for UNK). Our method OneRing-S is just a source model trained with 2 CE losses without any extra modules for domain generalization. We found it remarkable that the simple method (only applying Eq.1 during source training) has higher UNK accuracy (and comparable H) than those methods with complex open-set detection modules. E.g. unknown samples generation and manually set threshold to reject the unknown samples. 

### reference
 
[1] Saito, Kuniaki, and Kate Saenko. "Ovanet: One-vs-all network for universal domain adaptation." ICCV 2021.\
[2] Chang, Wanxing, et al. "Unified Optimal Transport Framework for Universal Domain Adaptation." NeurIPS 2022.\
[3] Liang, Jian, et al. "UMAD: Universal Model Adaptation under Domain and Category Shift." arXiv preprint arXiv:2112.08553 (2021).\
[4] Chen, Liang, et al. "Geometric Anchor Correspondence Mining With Uncertainty Modeling for Universal Domain Adaptation." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2022.\
[5] Li, Guangrui, et al. "Domain consensus clustering for universal domain adaptation." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2021.\
[6] Fu, Bo, et al. "Learning to detect open classes for universal domain adaptation." European Conference on Computer Vision. Springer, Cham, 2020.\
[7] Nath Kundu, Jogendra, et al. "Subsidiary Prototype Alignment for Universal Domain Adaptation." NeurIPS 2022\
